Official recruitment profile — Ayoub Messelmani, middle blocker, 197 cm, Tunisia national team volleyball.
Ayoub Messelmani · Middle Blocker · Tunisia National Team

Ayoub Messelmani is the impenetrable wall and the bright future of Tunisian volleyball. From his continental achievements in Morocco 2022 to his global emergence in China 2025, Ayoub has proven that ambition knows no bounds. With his skills as a modern Central player characterized by height and speed, he continues to write an inspiring success story that began in the "Capital of Volleyball," Kelibia, and reached the world's most prestigious arenas, confirming his status as a vital asset to the Tunisian National Team.

Ayoub Messelmani remains deeply loyal to his first school, the Club Olympique de Kélibia (COK). His journey as an ambitious Central player began at the Aissa Ben Nasr arena in Kelibia. Through hard work and discipline, Ayoub contributed to enriching his club's record with titles across youth categories (Cadets and Juniors) and has now become a cornerstone of the senior team. He represents the continuity of the legendary generation in Kelibia, blending local excellence with the international experience he gained from the courts of Morocco and China.

Beyond the glory of the title, the 2024 victory in Tunisia served as the essential gateway to the world stage. By winning the African Championship, Ayoub and his teammates officially secured their qualification for the 2025 World Championship in China. His leadership and defensive mastery during this tournament were crucial in ensuring that the Tunisian flag would fly high among the world's elite in the upcoming global competition.

In 2024, Ayoub Messelmani reached the pinnacle of African volleyball by leading the "Carthage Eagles" to win the U21 African Nations Championship on home soil in Tunisia. As a dominant Middle Blocker, his clinical performance at the net was the driving force behind the team's gold medal victory. This achievement solidified his status as one of the finest talents in the continent, bringing the trophy back to Tunisia and setting a new standard for his career.

The road to the 2024 title was paved two years earlier during the U19 African Nations Championship in Morocco. In the 2022 edition, Ayoub emerged as a standout young talent as the team fought their way to the semi-finals. His performance was individually recognized on the continental stage, where he was awarded the Second Best Blocker of the tournament. Standing at nearly two meters tall, this achievement was the first major step in his rapid development, providing the high-stakes international exposure that shaped his resilience and tactical growth for the world stage.

Ayoub’s impact peaked during crucial tournament fixtures where his individual statistics stood out on the global stage. In the high-stakes match against Colombia, he delivered a masterclass by scoring 6 points, including a staggering 4 points directly from blocks. He continued this momentum in the game against Ukraine, contributing 5 vital points. Competing against the likes of Argentina and France, Ayoub proved that he could maintain high-level efficiency against the world's most sophisticated offensive systems.

In the heart of the Chinese arenas, Ayoub demonstrated exceptional technical prowess and tactical discipline. His ability to read the opponent's setter allowed him to execute perfect "closed blocks" against world-class powerhouses like Italy and Brazil. Beyond defense, he proved to be a versatile offensive threat, utilizing quick "A" and "B" attacks from the middle of the net. His mobility and lateral speed in covering the entire width of the court showcased the modern standard of an elite Central player.

The year 2025 marked the most significant milestone in Ayoub Messelmani’s international career as he represented the Tunisian National Team at the FIVB Men's U21 World Championship in China. Standing at 197 cm and wearing jersey number 14, Messelmani established himself as a formidable Middle Blocker (Central). From the opening matches, his presence at the net was felt by elite global teams, where his height and wingspan created a "no-fly zone" for opposing attackers.
Volleyball Player at Club Olympique de Kélibia (COK).
